reason: Selected reproducibility study supports an inferred clean-environment check; causal language and model-training explanations in discussion are not treated as established.

candidates.title: Test generated projects from a clean declared environment
candidates.rule: Before accepting a generated project as reproducible, build and run it in a clean environment using its declared dependencies, recording code errors separately from missing packages.
candidates.passage: only 10.5% of failures are due to missing dependency declarations.
candidates.location: Discussion and conclusion; abstract study design
candidates.finding: Across three hundred generated projects, 68.3% run out of the box; most classified failures are code-generation errors rather than missing dependency declarations. The clean-environment check is inferred as a workflow safeguard, not an ablated mitigation.
models: Gemini coding agents; pinned versions not established in inspected sections
workloads: One hundred standardized project prompts in Python, JavaScript and Java
candidates.conditions: Study distinguishes declared, working and runtime dependencies. Transitive package expansion is measured on successful projects.
candidates.limitations: Observed agent/language differences are a historical sample, not stable specializations. Transitive dependencies are normal and do not all need manual direct declarations. Training-data explanations and productivity extrapolations are speculative.
candidates.validation_test: Create a fresh container from the declared manifest/lockfile, build and run meaningful project checks, then classify missing declarations, version conflicts and code failures; verify a second clean reproduction.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
